findings.title: clamp labels exact boundary values as out of range
findings.cause: The floor and ceil checks use <= and >= even though the docstring and argument text describe clamping only when the value is smaller than floor or larger than ceil.
findings.impact: Values exactly equal to a configured threshold get misleading '<' or '>' tokens, so boundary-safe values are reported as under/over the limit.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:473 documents clamp(0.99, format='{:.0%}', ceil=0.99) as '99%'
src/humanize/number.py:509 uses value <= floor and src/humanize/number.py:512 uses value >= ceil
doctest on humanize.number reports clamp(0.99, format='{:.0%}', ceil=0.99): expected '99%', got '>99%'
focused probe returned clamp(0.01, floor=0.01) -> '<0.01'
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import doctest, humanize.number
print(doctest.testmod(humanize.number))
PY

findings.title: intcomma does not add thousands separators to negative numbers
findings.cause: After conversion, the grouping loop applies a regex anchored to a digit at the start of the string, so values beginning with '-' never match.
findings.impact: Negative integers, floats, and numeric strings are returned without grouping, producing inconsistent formatting for balances, deltas, and signed quantities.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:167 stores the signed string form in orig
src/humanize/number.py:172 only matches ^(\d+)(\d{3})
focused probe returned intcomma(-1234567) -> '-1234567'
focused probe returned intcomma('-1234567.89') -> '-1234567.89'
tests/test_number.py covers positive intcomma values and non-finite values but no negative intcomma case
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
print(humanize.intcomma(-1234567))
print(humanize.intcomma('-1234567.89'))
PY

findings.title: fractional corrupts signs for negative fractions
findings.cause: The function truncates with int(number), then removes the numerator sign for proper fractions and leaves a negative numerator beside a negative whole part for mixed fractions.
findings.impact: Negative fractional values are either converted to positive values or rendered as awkward invalid-looking mixed fractions, changing the represented quantity.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:370 uses int(number), which truncates -0.25 to 0
src/humanize/number.py:379-380 applies abs(numerator) when there is no whole part
src/humanize/number.py:382 emits the signed numerator directly for mixed numbers
focused probe returned fractional(-0.25) -> '1/4'
focused probe returned fractional(-1.25) -> '-1 -1/4'
tests/test_number.py covers positive fractional values and non-finite values but no negative fractional case
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
print(humanize.fractional(-0.25))
print(humanize.fractional(-1.25))
PY

findings.title: non-finite numeric time inputs raise OverflowError instead of falling back
findings.cause: naturaldelta catches ValueError and TypeError around int(value) and datetime.timedelta construction, while _date_and_delta catches ValueError and TypeError around round(value); neither catches OverflowError from float infinity.
findings.impact: Public time humanizers crash on math.inf instead of returning the input string or a controlled non-finite representation, despite nearby tests asserting graceful behavior for string 'NaN'.
evidence: src/humanize/time.py:148-153 catches ValueError and TypeError but not OverflowError
src/humanize/time.py:86-91 catches ValueError and TypeError but not OverflowError
src/humanize/time.py:112-116 says values that cannot be converted are returned unchanged
focused probe returned naturaldelta(math.inf) !! OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
focused probe returned naturaltime(math.inf) !! OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
tests/test_time.py covers the string 'NaN' path but no float('inf') or float('nan') path

findings.title: naturalsize mishandles NaN and infinity
findings.cause: The function converts input to float and proceeds into integer/logarithm formatting without checking math.isfinite.
findings.impact: NaN raises ValueError, while infinity is formatted as a finite maximum suffix value such as 'inf QB', which is not a meaningful filesize.
evidence: src/humanize/filesize.py:90 converts value with float(value)
src/humanize/filesize.py:96-101 converts abs_bytes through integer/log suffix selection with no finite guard
focused probe returned naturalsize(math.nan) !! ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer
focused probe returned naturalsize(math.inf) -> 'inf QB'
tests/test_filesize.py has no non-finite filesize cases

findings.title: natural_list renders an empty list as the literal string None
findings.cause: The zero-length branch returns the literal string 'None' instead of an empty natural list representation.
findings.impact: Empty collections in UI or reports are rendered as if the value were None or the text item 'None', which can mislead callers and users.
evidence: src/humanize/lists.py:31-32 returns 'None' when len(items) == 0
src/humanize/lists.py:25-29 describes producing a string with commas and 'and', not a sentinel value
focused probe returned natural_list([]) -> 'None'
tests/test_lists.py covers one, two, and three items but no empty list
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
print(humanize.natural_list([]))
PY
